source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies unrestricted designs and estimators for finite-population SATE, reduces the binary problem to a two-parameter experiment, obtains an Airy second-order expansion, and attains minimax risk with Bernoulli randomization and nonlinear shrinkage.
Independent assignment is minimax for bounded finite-population potential outcomes, including after extension to arbitrary estimators, with a generally nonlinear optimal estimator.
The paper gives exact matched-pair binary randomization inference under within-pair coin flips and reduces the worst compatible allocation to a boundary corner.
The paper gives exact binary ATE intervals with O(log n) tests for balanced Bernoulli and matched-pairs designs, and O(n^2) tests for general Bernoulli designs.
The paper proves permutation-group averaging from a fixed assignment vector and estimator, then treats simple optimal schemes only under further assumptions.
Among stratified schemes treating units with probability one half, a matched-pair design maximizes ATE precision; baseline-outcome pairing is an identified special case.
The cited article exists as the stated JRSSB paper on minimax-variance randomization and design-based inference.
